evidence: books/served-catalog.lisp:3373-3380: (let ((number (if (equal direction :next) (fn-scat-next-number group current v fn-cat) ...))) (if (posp number) (fn-nntp-article-response session (fn-scat-available-article group number v fn-arena fn-cat) number :stat t group fn-arena) ...)). The next number comes from availability (books/nntp-projection.lisp:61-68, fn-nntp-article-number: posp number, <= 2^31-1, fn-nntp-article-idp) and does not consider reclamation. fn-nntp-article-response then checks tombstones first (books/nntp-responses.lisp:117-121: (if (fn-nntp-article-tombstonep article fn-arena) (fn-nntp-single session (if updatep (fn-proto-text * :reclaimed) ...)))). It returns the old `session`, so the cursor stays where it was. books/protocol-table.lisp:569 and :547 list `(423 :refused :reader :reclaimed "423 article reclaimed")` as a NEXT/LAST reply.
fix: In fn-nntp-group-next-number / -last-number and their -cat and index twins, make NEXT/LAST skip numbers whose stored payload is a tombstone (or use a 'servable' predicate that excludes reclaimed articles), so the step reaches the next live article. Answer the current-article form of a reclaimed article with 420. Remove 423 from the NEXT/LAST rows of the protocol table.
reviewer: fn-scat-next-number (books/served-catalog.lisp:3309) uses fn-scv-first-p, and fn-scv-keptp (books/served-catalog-view.lisp:54-63) checks only that the article is visible and has a msgid. It never checks for a tombstone, so a reclaimed article is the next number. fn-nntp-next-or-last-cat (:3369-3383) passes it to fn-nntp-article-response with updatep t. The tombstone arm (books/nntp-responses.lisp:117-121) returns the unchanged session with 423, so the cursor never moves past it, and every repeated NEXT/LAST hits the same tombstone. OVER does skip tombstones (served-catalog.lisp:656, 2705), so the difference is real. Reclaim does reach the served node: it runs offline (requirements.json:5429), and the node serves the tombstones once it restarts. The 423 for NEXT/LAST (protocol-table.lisp:547, 569) is outside RFC 3977 6.1.3/6.1.4, which allow 223/412/420/421.
scenario: Group g holds articles 1, 2 and 3, and 2 is reclaimed (D13 keeps its membership and number). A reader runs GROUP g (cursor 1), then NEXT. fn-scat-next-number returns 2, which is a tombstone, so the reply is "423 article reclaimed" and the cursor stays at 1. Every later NEXT returns the same 423, so article 3 can never be reached with NEXT. A client that loops on NEXT until 421 never terminates. LAST from 3 is stuck the same way. RFC 3977 sections 6.1.3 and 6.1.4 allow only 223/412/420/421 (or 422) for these commands, so 423 is also outside the RFC response set. The current-article form of ARTICLE/HEAD/BODY/STAT, where updatep is t, answers 423 for a reclaimed current article where section 6.2.1.2 allows only 420. This differs from the known 'GROUP counts reclaimed articles' item: that one is about the counts, this one is cursor navigation.
title: NEXT/LAST land on a reclaimed article, answer 423 and never move the cursor, so a reader cannot step past a tombstone
